There used to be dumps at the edge of every town.
The motel turned out to be a total dump.
I'm not eating in that dump.
They fixed up the old dump and sold it for a profit.

senses.head: A place where people leave trash and unwanted things
examples: He took the old couch to the dump.
The dump charges by the pound now.
There used to be dumps at the edge of every town.

senses.head: A dirty, unpleasant, run-down place
examples: The motel turned out to be a total dump.
I'm not eating in that dump.
They fixed up the old dump and sold it for a profit.

entries.meaning: A lot where wrecked cars and scrap metal are kept. ---
examples: He found the part at a junkyard.
A dog barked behind the junkyard fence.
The junkyards out on Route 9 buy scrap by the ton.
entries.contrast: Americans say junkyard; the British say scrapyard.

entries.meaning: A furnace built to burn waste. ---
examples: The hospital burns its waste in an incinerator.
Neighbors fought the new incinerator for years.
Old apartment buildings had incinerators in the basement.

entries.meaning: The act of getting rid of waste properly. ---
examples: The city handles disposal of household waste.
Proper disposal of paint means a special drop-off.
Disposal of the old mattress cost forty dollars.

entries.meaning: The truck that collects household waste from the curb. ---
examples: The garbage truck wakes us up at six.
He missed the garbage truck by five minutes.
Two garbage trucks work this route.

entries.meaning: The day of the week when waste is collected on a street. ---
examples: Tomorrow is trash day, so put the cans out.
Trash day moves to Wednesday on holiday weeks.
We have two trash days in the summer.

entries.meaning: A shaft in a building that carries garbage down to a bin. ---
examples: The trash chute is at the end of the hall.
Something's stuck in the trash chute again.
The trash chutes are locked after ten at night.
entries.contrast: Chute sounds like shoot.

entries.meaning: Someone who drops trash in a public place. ---
examples: Don't be a litterbug — there's a can right there.
The sign calls out litterbugs with a two-hundred-dollar fine.
A few litterbugs ruin the whole beach.

entries.meaning: Waste material; in British English, what Americans call trash. ---
examples: Put the rubbish out by the gate.
The yard was full of rubbish and broken glass.
He said the whole story was rubbish.
entries.contrast: Mainly British for trash; Americans use it to mean nonsense.

entries.meaning: A person employed by a city to collect and handle waste. ---
examples: A sanitation worker waved at the kids from the truck.
Sanitation workers got a new contract in June.
His father was a sanitation worker for thirty years.

entries.meaning: Someone whose job is picking up household waste. ---
examples: The garbage collector left a note on the can.
Garbage collectors don't take yard waste.
He worked as a garbage collector right out of high school.

entries.meaning: A person who cleans and takes care of a building. ---
examples: The custodian unlocked the gym for us.
Ask the custodian for a mop.
The school kept two custodians on the night shift.

entries.meaning: A woman employed to clean rooms in a house or hotel. ---
examples: The maid comes in to make up the room around ten.
They hired a maid twice a month.
The hotel maids were pushing carts down the hall.
entries.contrast: Sounds exactly like made.

entries.meaning: A person paid to clean and run a household. ---
examples: Their housekeeper comes on Tuesdays.
The housekeeper left a note about the laundry.
The hotel has housekeepers on every floor.

entries.meaning: A woman hired to clean a home or office. ---
examples: The cleaning lady comes every other Friday.
We leave the key under the mat for the cleaning lady.
The building hires cleaning ladies through an agency.

entries.meaning: A company you pay to send people to clean your home or office. ---
examples: We use a cleaning service once a month.
The cleaning service brings its own supplies.
She called three cleaning services for quotes.

entries.meaning: The work of cleaning a home from top to bottom. ---
examples: Saturday is for housecleaning.
Housecleaning takes her most of the day.
He does the housecleaning and she cooks.
entries.contrast: Written as one word; the verb phrase is clean house.

entries.meaning: A thorough cleaning of a whole house, done once a year. ---
examples: We're doing spring cleaning this weekend.
Spring cleaning means the windows too.
She got through half the spring cleaning before it rained.

entries.meaning: The quality of being tidy and well arranged. ---
examples: Her desk is a model of neatness.
They grade on neatness as well as spelling.
There's a neatness to the way he folds everything.

entries.meaning: The habit of keeping everything in its place. ---
examples: His tidiness drives his roommate crazy.
The apartment was spotless, but the tidiness felt cold.
Tidiness is the first thing she looks for in a sublet.

entries.meaning: Extreme dirt and neglect in the place where someone lives.
examples: The family was living in squalor.
Inspectors found squalor in half the units.
He wrote about the squalor of the old tenements.
